title: Myth vs. Fact: Flushing Hot Water Clears Grease Clogs
description: Many homeowners believe running hot water down the sink while dumping fats, oils, and grease prevents plumbing clogs. In reality, hot water only keeps grease liquefied briefly while it enters the drain. As the warm grease travels further down cold wall-enclosed or underground pipes, it quickly cools, coats the pipe walls, and solidifies. Over time, these layers trap other debris and choke off wastewater flow. Professional plumbers advise scraping cooking oils into solid trash containers or grease traps rather than washing them down the drain line.

Myth vs. Fact: Flushing Hot Water Clears Grease Clogs

Many homeowners believe running hot water down the sink while dumping fats, oils, and grease prevents plumbing clogs. In reality, hot water only keeps grease liquefied briefly while it enters the drain. As the warm grease travels further down cold wall-enclosed or underground pipes, it quickly cools, coats the pipe walls, and solidifies. Over time, these layers trap other debris and choke off wastewater flow. Professional plumbers advise scraping cooking oils into solid trash containers or grease traps rather than washing them down the drain line.
